# Pranay Gupta

> Co-founder and CTO of Argon Robotics (San Francisco). Works on robot learning: simulation that holds up against real robots, fast manipulation policies, RL post-training, and LLMs that edit robot policy weights.

- [Homepage](https://codnay.github.io/): about, featured work, interests, experience
- [Writing](https://codnay.github.io/blog/): all posts, also as RSS at https://codnay.github.io/blog/feed.xml

## Posts

- [What the fuck is the sim-to-real gap?](https://codnay.github.io/blog/sim-to-real-gap/) (2026-11-07): We found 20 bugs in open-source physics engines. The three that hurt large-scale robot training most, and the rest in one picture.
- [Robots need their own wind tunnel](https://codnay.github.io/blog/robots-need-their-own-wind-tunnel/) (2026-11-07): Physics engines were built for games, controllers and walking. Robot hands need something else, so we are building it.
- [Can frontier LLMs fix robots by editing their weights?](https://codnay.github.io/blog/llms-fix-robots-by-editing-weights/) (2026-11-04): We asked Opus to improve π0.5 by editing its weights directly, with no gradient training. Laundry folding went from 51% to 75%, and a mahjong task from 23% to 36%.
- [Discovery-0: zero-shot sim-to-real](https://www.argonrobotics.ai/discovery) (2026-10-21): A model trained only on trajectories from our simulated kitchens closed a commercial dishwasher in a live customer kitchen, with no real-world data for the task.
- [The Turing test for virtual worlds](https://www.argonrobotics.ai/simreal) (2026-10-14): Ten frames from the same robot stations, some from the real robot and some from our simulation of it. A game: can you tell which is which?
- [Scaling and speeding up robots in the real world](https://codnay.github.io/blog/scaling-and-speeding-up-robots-in-the-real-world/) (2026-09-18): Three levers that make robot policies run nearly four times faster than the remote-teleoperation data they learned from, without losing accuracy.
